postTitle: Real Returns: How to Tell if Your Portfolio Is Really Performing
topic: A return only means something next to a comparison with the same mix

assumptions.notes: Lesson example: a portfolio of 60% global shares and 40% bonds rose 12%; a widely quoted share index rose 24%; a 60/40 blended index returned about 11%.

The news index tracks only shares, so the mix differs.

caption.instagram:
Your investments made 12%. The index in the news made 24%. Did you do badly?

The example: a portfolio of 60% global shares and 40% bonds rose 12% in a year when a widely quoted share index rose 24%. Next to that index it looks poor. Next to a blend of 60% shares and 40% bonds, which returned about 11%, it did slightly better.

A fair comparison holds the same kinds of investments in the same proportions. Even then, a small gap in one year is usually noise. A gap that lasts, with a cause such as high fees or a mix that has drifted, is the kind people look into.
